title: Epigenetic active inference is indispensable for patterning beyond genetic encoding

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Epigenetic active inference is indispensable for patterning beyond genetic encoding

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although aspects of the target morphology are genetically encoded in the parameters of cells' generative models, epigenetic processes (active inference) are indispensable for patterning, consistent with the regenerative target morphology of planaria being permanently alterable (to two heads) by a brief modification of electric synapses.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Conclusion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It may be worth concluding that although aspects of the target morphology are genetically encoded (in the parameters of the generative models); epigenetic processes (active inference) are indispensable for patterning.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Friston K, Levin M, Sengupta B, Pezzulo G, “Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation”, Journal of the Royal Society, Interface (2015), doi:10.1098/rsif.2014.1383; section “Conclusion”. Scope: Morphogenesis and regeneration, e.g. planarian regeneration

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-place-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Ablation in the model and selected planarian findings address restricted consequences of dynamic state updates. They do not discriminate the active-inference interpretation or establish indispensability across morphogenesis.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define epigenetic active inference as signalling-dependent state updates and compare morphogenesis models with those updates disabled while genetic parameters remain fixed. Existing planarian perturbation results can test persistence of target-shape changes, but not universal indispensability.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Active inference' is not uniquely identifiable from ordinary regulation.

Indispensability over all patterning systems is too broad for available data.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.25
analysis feasibility: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The indispensable-process claim equates epigenetic patterning with active inference and then cites stable planarian target change as agreement. The same phenotype is expected from any account in which a transient physiological perturbation rewrites a non-genetic target. No existing measurement separates the free-energy identification from those rivals.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Permanent two-headed regeneration after a brief gap-junction change shows that a non-genetic physiological state can reset target anatomy. That observation is also what a bioelectric-memory description predicts, so it does not single out active inference as the indispensable process.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Active inference is identified with epigenetic patterning by definition in the sentence.

The planarian phenotype is compatible with several physiological accounts.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.12
data adequacy: 0.1
operationalizability: 0.28
data existence: 0.12
